The Gruen Transfer is consuming the internet
Have you ever walked into a supermarket, pharmacy, or department store looking to buy a specific item, only to find the layout confusing? Perhaps you ended up aimlessly strolling around, purchasing other items? This is deliberate, and known as the Gruen Transfer.
The 'Transfer' part is the moment that you, as a consumer surrounded by a deliberately confusing layout, lose track of your original intentions.
We've all experienced it, and now it's starting to consume the internet. It first appeared on Facebook, with the introduction of the feed. Originally intended as a way to simplify updates from your friends, and hold your attention captive for longer. However somewhere along the line, the feed became more than that. Facebook now feels more confusing than my local department store, and my original reason for visiting (keeping up to date with friends & family) is quickly forgotten. The last time I checked Facebook, maybe 10% of my feed was updates from friends. The rest was a combination of ads, memes, and influencer marketing videos, leaving me doom scrolling endlessly.
This isn't relegated to Facebook though, or even social media. So many websites are now designed to disorient you upon visiting, so that you start acting impulsively. This can even happen in a relatively benign way - who hasn't looked up something on Wikipedia and fell down a rabbit hole that ended looking at a
list of animals awarded human credentials
?
It pops up in other areas as well, closely associated with several UX dark patterns. If you've tried to permanently delete your account from any major social network, youâll know what I mean. It is utterly confusing to find and navigate to the page you need, and the site will desperately conjole you into doing something other than deleting your account. It's the same for trying to alter your insurance policy, cancel subscriptions, spend frequent flyer miles, and so on...
I wonder where all this will end? There must be a point at which the friction generated by needless complexity has a detrimental effect. A kind of
Laffer Curve
of web design.
In the EU, it is a legal requirement to allow your customers the same method, with the same number of steps and complexity, for canceling as for subscribing. So if it takes 10 seconds to fill in a form online to get subscribed, they need to offer the same ease of use for canceling.
I like this idea of âcomplexityâ as a measure for legislation. Now if only they could apply the same thing to my local Boots when I'm trying to buy toothpaste.

data.title: Mark Zuckerberg says social media is over
data.author: FinnLobsien
data.article_summary:
文章讨论了社交网络的演变及其在反垄断案件中的争议。文章指出，过去十年中，社交媒体从连接朋友、分享个人动态的平台，逐渐转变为以娱乐和信息传播为主的媒介，用户看到的更多是名人内容、新闻聚合和AI生成内容，而非朋友的帖子。Facebook创始人马克·扎克伯格在Meta的反垄断审判中承认了这一变化，强调公司现在更多关注娱乐和全球资讯。

联邦贸易委员会（F.T.C.）指控Meta在“个人社交网络服务”行业中维持非法垄断，部分通过收购Instagram和WhatsApp等竞争对手。然而，F.T.C.对社交媒体行业的定义模糊，其反垄断案曾在2021年被驳回。Meta辩称，如今的社交媒体已演变为广泛的内容消费平台，任何公司都无法独占。

F.T.C.的指控基于多年前批准的商业交易，但行业已发生巨变，使其案件不够严密。技术分析师认为F.T.C.的行业定义不准确，难以证明Meta的垄断造成消费者伤害或减少创新。WhatsApp和Instagram在被收购后用户大幅增长，也使得F.T.C.的指控难以成立。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Meta（Facebook）从社交网络向内容消费平台的转型及其影响

不同观点：
• flkiwi、throw0101d、jader201等认为，Facebook/Meta为了迎合华尔街和追求盈利，主动改变了平台的性质，从以社交为主转向以广告和内容消费为主。他们指出，这种变化并不是用户自然选择的结果，而是公司战略决策的后果。
• NullPointerWin、_hao、hcarvalhoalves等批评Meta目前的广告泛滥和内容质量下降，认为用户被迫接受大量无关的广告和低质内容，体验极差。
• curiousllama、pcarolan等指出，虽然Facebook提供了朋友专属的动态过滤功能，但由于用户不再频繁发布内容，该功能形同虚设。他们认为社交互动已经转移到其他平台如群聊中。
• 3np、JamesLeonis等认为，Meta试图通过扩大其市场定义来掩饰其垄断行为，并引用彼得·蒂尔的垄断理论，指出Meta正在采用类似的策略。
• Animats、jjulius等关注Meta的广告策略和用户流失问题，认为增加广告密度会导致用户体验下降，进而形成恶性循环。

补充讨论：
• seydor对Meta展示的数据提出质疑，认为用户观看非朋友内容的比例上升并不代表用户偏好，而是平台推送的结果。
• laweijfmvo将Meta的情况与Fox News类比，认为公司在法律压力下承认了一些不利的事实。

争议焦点：
• Meta的平台转型是否是用户需求驱动的，还是公司为了盈利而做出的战略选择。
• 广告密度的增加是否导致了用户体验的下降和平台的衰落。
• Meta是否在通过重新定义其市场来掩饰其垄断行为。

What, exactly, does a social network do? Is it a website that connects people with one another online, a digital gathering place where we can consume content posted by our friends? That’s certainly what it was in its heyday, in the two-thousands. Facebook was where you might find out that your friend was dating someone new, or that someone had thrown a party without inviting you. In the course of the past decade, though, social media has come to resemble something more like regular media. It’s where we find promotional videos created by celebrities, pundits shouting responses to the news, aggregated clips from pop culture, a rising tide of A.I.-generated slop, and other content designed to be broadcast to the largest number of viewers possible. The people we follow and the messages they post increasingly feel like needles in a digital haystack. Social media has become less social.
Facebook’s founder, Mark Zuckerberg, admitted as much during more than ten hours of testimony, over three days last week, in the opening phase of the Federal Trade Commission’s antitrust trial against Facebook’s parent company, Meta. The company, Zuckerberg said, has lately been involved in “the general idea of entertainment and learning about the world and discovering what’s going on.” This under-recognized shift away from interpersonal communication has been measured by the company itself. During the defense’s opening statement, Meta displayed a chart showing that the “percent of time spent viewing content posted by ‘friends’ ” has declined in the past two years, from twenty-two per cent to seventeen per cent on Facebook, and from eleven per cent to seven per cent on Instagram.
The F.T.C. is arguing that Meta maintained an illegal monopoly in the “personal social networking services” industry, in part by buying up Facebook’s competitors, such as Instagram, which the company acquired in 2012, and the messaging platform WhatsApp, which it acquired in 2014. But the F.T.C.’s definition of the social-media industry is hazy, and the antitrust case was already dismissed once, in 2021, partly because the “personal social networking services” market was too loosely defined. Meta’s counter-argument is, in a sense, that social media per se doesn’t exist now in the way that it did in the twenty-tens, and that what the company’s platforms are now known for—the digital consumption of all kinds of content—has become so widespread that no single company or platform can be said to monopolize it. In one of its slides at trial, Meta exhibited a graphic of a boxing ring showing the logos of Instagram, Facebook, and the various companies that Meta argues are competitors, including TikTok, YouTube, and Apple’s iMessage, though the F.T.C. doesn’t define any of those three as such. The company also used smartphone screenshots from the various apps to demonstrate how they’ve gravitated toward common formats: short video clips look similar on both Instagram and TikTok; messages look essentially the same in Instagram DMs as on Apple’s iMessage. Even as such similarities serve as helpful evidence for Meta’s defense, they also demonstrate how stultifying the entire online ecosystem has become. While in 2012 Facebook may have seemed singular and inescapable, now it looks like part of a crowded marketplace of apps competing to serve the same purpose.
The F.T.C.’s case, which originated during Donald Trump’s first term, entails reëvaluating business deals that it approved more than a decade ago, when the industry looked dramatically different. This makes the commission’s case less than airtight. Benedict Evans, an influential technology analyst, called the F.T.C.’s market definition of social networks “gerrymandering.” He told me, “By the F.T.C.’s definition, TikTok doesn’t compete with Facebook at all. Does that mean it would be O.K. for Facebook to buy TikTok?” Antitrust lawyers must prove that allegedly monopolistic practices cause consumer harm. In another antitrust case currently unfolding against Google, a court found that the company maintained a monopoly over parts of the online-advertising market by integrating its various automated advertising technologies, illegally privileging itself and harming its publishing customers by “reducing their revenue.” In the case of Meta, though, there is no price differential to point to—Meta’s platforms all allow users to access them for free—so the question of harm is less clear-cut.
The F.T.C. is arguing, instead, that Meta’s purported monopoly has led to a lack of innovation and to reduced consumer choice. But that, too, is difficult to prove in the case of Meta’s WhatsApp and Instagram acquisitions, because both sales occurred early in those companies’ life spans. • seydor对Meta展示的数据提出质疑，认为用户观看非朋友内容的比例上升并不代表用户偏好，而是平台推送的结果。
• laweijfmvo将Meta的情况与Fox News类比，认为公司在法律压力下承认了一些不利的事实。

争议焦点：
• Meta的平台转型是否是用户需求驱动的，还是公司为了盈利而做出的战略选择。
• 广告密度的增加是否导致了用户体验的下降和平台的衰落。
• Meta是否在通过重新定义其市场来掩饰其垄断行为。

data.title: Three things everyone should know about Vision Transformers
data.author: reqo
data.article_summary:
这篇文章讨论了视觉Transformer（Vision Transformers, ViTs）的三个重要发现：

1. 视觉Transformer的残差层通常是顺序处理的，但在一定程度上可以并行处理，且不显著影响精度。
2. 仅微调注意力层的权重即可使视觉Transformer适应更高分辨率和其他分类任务，从而节省计算资源，减少峰值内存消耗，并实现权重共享。
3. 添加基于MLP的块预处理层可以改善基于块掩码的Bert式自监督训练。

这些发现通过ImageNet-1k数据集验证，并在ImageNet-v2测试集上确认，同时在六个较小的数据集上测量了迁移性能。

Computer Science > Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition

Title:
Three things everyone should know about Vision Transformers
Authors:
Hugo Touvron
,
Matthieu Cord
,
Alaaeldin El-Nouby
,
Jakob Verbeek
,
Hervé Jégou
View a PDF of the paper titled Three things everyone should know about Vision Transformers, by Hugo Touvron and 4 other authors
View PDF
Abstract:
After their initial success in natural language processing, transformer architectures have rapidly gained traction in computer vision, providing state-of-the-art results for tasks such as image classification, detection, segmentation, and video analysis. We offer three insights based on simple and easy to implement variants of vision transformers. (1) The residual layers of vision transformers, which are usually processed sequentially, can to some extent be processed efficiently in parallel without noticeably affecting the accuracy. (2) Fine-tuning the weights of the attention layers is sufficient to adapt vision transformers to a higher resolution and to other classification tasks. This saves compute, reduces the peak memory consumption at fine-tuning time, and allows sharing the majority of weights across tasks. (3) Adding MLP-based patch pre-processing layers improves Bert-like self-supervised training based on patch masking. We evaluate the impact of these design choices using the ImageNet-1k dataset, and confirm our findings on the ImageNet-v2 test set. Transfer performance is measured across six smaller datasets.

data.title: Daily driving a Linux phone, but why?
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了作者尝试将Linux手机作为日常主力设备的体验和原因。相比Android手机，作者认为使用Linux手机并不是为了舒适或方便，而是一种对生活模式的反思和探索。尽管有人认为Linux手机在安全性和隐私方面不如Android或iOS，但Linux的开源特性提供了更高的隐私保护。文章还提到，虽然PinePhone Pro的硬件速度较慢，但对作者而言足够使用，并且它在便携性和音频接口方面优于作者的FairPhone。作者最终计划尝试在LG v40 Thinq上安装Linux系统，因为这是他最喜欢的Android手机，且硬件性能更好。不过，作者首先需要解决启动问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Linux手机的实用性、隐私性、安全性及其替代主流手机操作系统的潜力。

不同观点：
• [mft_] 认为极端追求隐私和安全（如运行Linux手机）可能会影响正常生活功能，带来更多不便。他通过个人经历说明，过度追求隐私可能导致人际关系难以维持。
• [greatgib] 推荐Furiphone作为日常使用的Linux手机，认为其功能齐全，尤其是能运行Android应用且具备控制权限的能力，但指出部分应用仍需依赖Google服务。
• [codethief] 对Linux手机的安全性表示担忧，指出开源系统可能面临依赖性问题的风险，并引用SpectrumOS开发者的经历来说明构建安全操作系统的困难。
• [mpol] 询问PostmarketOS作为日常驱动的可行性，表示目前使用Sailfish OS满足基本需求，但对Linux手机持开放态度。
• [Animats] 使用无Google服务的Android手机，通过F-Droid获取应用，认为这是一种可行的隐私保护方案。
• [INTPenis] 回顾过去使用Linux手机的经历，认为早期的Linux手机系统（如Maemo/Meego）不够成熟，但赞赏当前Android系统的成熟。
• [its-kostya] 认为现代手机的强大计算能力使得运行任意软件成为可能，但软件的臃肿化使得这种自由受限。
• [Jhsto] 计划通过使用Linux手机来管理智能手机成瘾，并逐步摆脱Apple生态系统，但认为某些应用（如旅行和密码管理）仍需依赖其他设备。
• [xcircle] 推荐Liberux，这是一个欧洲开发的Linux手机项目。
• [butz] 询问能够运行Linux且具备基本功能的最小现代手机。
• [OsrsNeedsf2P] 对Linux桌面和手机的普及持悲观态度，但仍看到其潜力。
• [Y_Y] 强烈批评Android和iOS的商业模式，认为其对用户体验造成负面影响，并支持使用Linux手机作为替代。
• [tmtvl] 使用Ubuntu Touch作为日常驱动，满足大部分需求，但通过Waydroid运行WhatsApp等必要应用。
• [yndoendo] 正在寻求替代Google的Linux手机，目前使用Fairphone和\e\OS，期待FuriPhone，并对美国政府政策影响科技选择表示关注。

补充讨论：
• Linux手机的定义和与Android的区别是争议焦点之一。例如，[Tepix] 认为AOSP Android手机已经具备许多Linux手机的特性，质疑追求纯Linux手机的必要性。
• 用户对Linux手机的期望主要集中在隐私保护、安全性和自由运行开源软件的能力。
• 实际使用中，Linux手机面临应用兼容性和功能不全的问题，部分用户通过Waydroid等工具解决。
• 对Linux手机的市场普及和对抗主流科技公司的潜力存在不同看法，部分用户持乐观态度，认为将受益于科技转型。

43779766.article_content:
Daily driving a Linux phone, but why?
April 24, 2025
431 words
As a follow-up to
a post
describing what would be involved for me to daily drive a Linux phone, you could wonder why this would in any way be better than Android. After all, an Android phone will still be needed and remain charged, even though I wonât need to carry it around.
Itâs like using a paper notebook and calendar. Itâs not about whatâs most comfortable or easiest. Itâs about a journey to question how we are forced to live our lives and to learn how to live (marginally) differently. Itâs also about a better balance between security and privacy. Many will point out that a Linux phone is less secure than Android or iOS, but that highly depends on your personal threat model. Linux phones and their apps are all open-source and do not depend on ads or surveillance to sustain some nefarious business model, which means there is much privacy to be won.
My LGv40 Thinq in fastboot mode
The PinePhone Proâs hardware is slow. Very slow. It has been called âbeyond outdatedâ on Reddit, though that doesnât mean much to me, seeing that there are four computers from the 1980s less than two meters to my left when Iâm writing this. But no matter how fast a phone is, it will never be as fast as my paper calendar or notebook. The PinePhone Pro fast enough to have Firefox play videos or music without interruption, and the navigation and running apps have no problem keeping up with me. And while an app is loading, at least itâs not overstimulating me.
The PinePhone Pro also has a few advantages over my FairPhone, to be honest. Itâs lighter and smaller, for one thing, and it has a proper 3.5mm headphone jack. I have a USB-C to 3.5mm cable for my FairPhone, but I always have to re-insert it a few times before itâs picked up. This just works.
As mentioned in the other post, Iâm not planning on using the PinePhone Pro. I unlocked the bootloader of my LGv40 Thinq some time ago, and it has a Snapdragon 845 SDM845 SoC, so I can use one of PostmarketOSâs
mainline guides
. Iâd love to use this phone again. Of all my Android phones, it was my
favourite
. Itâs even smaller than the PinePhone Pro while simultaneously having a slightly bigger screen, itâs much faster too and still has a 3.5mm jack. It also has wireless charging, excellent cameras and a fingerprint reader on the back
But letâs see first if I can get it to boot.

data.title: MCP on AWS Lambda with MCPEngine
data.author: simba-k
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了如何使用MCPEngine在AWS Lambda上部署MCP服务器。MCP（Model Context Protocol）是让大型语言模型（LLM）调用外部工具的协议，但现有实现多为本地运行，且依赖Server-Sent Events（SSE）进行流式传输，不适合无状态环境如AWS Lambda。MCPEngine解决了这些问题，支持HTTP流式传输，兼容Lambda，并提供认证、打包等功能。文章通过三个例子演示了如何构建和部署无状态、有状态（使用RDS）和认证（使用OIDC）的MCP服务器，所有例子均可在Lambda上运行，无需自定义代理。部署可通过Terraform自动化或手动完成。
data.comments_summary:

Model Context Protocol (MCP) is quickly becoming the standard for enabling LLMs to call external tools. Itâs built around clean, declarative tool definitionsâbut most current implementations fall short of being production-ready. Every official MCP server in the Anthropic repo, for instance, runs locally and communicates over stdio. Even the few that support HTTP rely on Server-Sent Events (SSE) for streaming. This introduces stateful behavior, requiring persistent TCP connections, complicating retries, and ultimately making it incompatible with stateless environments like AWS Lambda.
Weâve written more about these limitations, and how weâve addressed them with MCPEngine.
AWS Lambda offers instant scalability, no server management, and efficient, event-driven execution. We built native support for it in MCPEngine, so that MCP tools can run cleanly and reliably in serverless environments.
MCPEngine
is an open-source implementation of MCP that supports streamable HTTP alongside SSE, making it compatible with Lambda. It also includes first-class support for authentication, packaging, and other capabilities to build and deploy production-grade MCP servers.
This post walks through building three progressively more realistic examples:
A stateless MCP server with a single tool
A stateful version using RDS and a context handler
An authenticated version using OIDC (Google or Cognito)
All three run entirely in Lambda, don't require a custom agent, and are MCP-spec compliant.
1. Build and Deploy a Stateless Weather MCP API
You can follow along on
GitHub here for the full project
.
1.1 Defining the MCP Server
We'll start with a single tool called get_weather. It takes a city name and returns a canned string response. There's no state or external API call â just enough to validate end-to-end behavior with a live LLM.
Install the Python SDK:
pip install mcpengine[cli,lambda]
Create a file called app.py:
from
mcpengine
import
MCPEngine
engine = MCPEngine()
@engine.tool()
def
get_weather
(
city:
str
) ->
str
:
"""Return the current weather for a given city.
"""
return
f"The weather in
{city}
is sunny and 72Â°F."
â
handler = engine.get_lambda_handler()
What this does:
@engine.tool
registers the function with the MCP manifest. The function name (`get_weather`) becomes the tool name exposed to the LLM.
The docstring is exposed in the manifest and shown to the LLM during tool selection.
handler is the AWS Lambda-compatible entry point. No glue code required â Lambda is configured to look for a global named handler and MCPEngine handles the request lifecycle.
1.2 Deploying to Lambda
You can deploy this manually or use Terraform to automate setup.
Option 1: Terraform
If you want to skip most of the boilerplate, we provide Terraform scripts that:
Creates an ECR repository to host the image
Provisions the Lambda function and IAM roles
Exposes it via a Function URL
You can run it in the directory by calling:
terraform apply
Grab the ECR repository url and Lambda function name from the terraform output:
export
REPOSITORY_URL=$(terraform output -raw repository_url)
export
FUNCTION_NAME=$(terraform output -raw lambda_name)
And then build, tag, and push the image:
docker build --platform=linux/amd64 --provenance=
false
-t mcp-lambda:latest .
docker tag mcp-lambda
${REPOSITORY_URL}
:latest
docker push
${REPOSITORY_URL}
:latest
Finally, weâll update the Lambda with this new image:
aws lambda update-function-code \
--function-name
${FUNCTION_NAME}
\
--image-uri
${REPOSITORY_URL}
:latest
And the application will be running. Once deployed, you can tear it down with:
terraform destroy
Option 2: From Scratch
If you prefer to deploy manually:
Step 1: Dockerize the Server
FROM
public.ecr.aws/lambda/python:
3.12
# Set working directory in the container
WORKDIR
/var/task
# Copy application code
COPY
. .
# Install dependencies
RUN
pip install --system --no-cache-dir .
# Expose port for the server
EXPOSE
8000
# Command to run the web server
CMD
[
"weather.server.handler"
]
Then:
docker build --platform=linux/amd64 --provenance=
false
-t mcp-lambda .
Step 2: Push to ECR
docker tag mcp-lambda:latest <your-ecr-url>/mcp-lambda:latest
docker push <your-ecr-url>/mcp-lambda:latest
Step 3: Deploy to Lambda
aws lambda create-function \
--function-name mcp-lambda \
--package-type Image \
--code ImageUri=<your-ecr-url>/mcp-lambda:latest \
--role arn:aws:iam::<account-id>:role/<lambda-role>
Step 4: Add permissions for Lambda
aws iam create-role \
--role-name lambda-container-execution \
--assume-role-policy-document
'{
"Version": "2012-10-17",
"Statement": [
{
"Effect": "Allow",
"Principal": {
"Service": "lambda.amazonaws.com"
},
"Action": "sts:AssumeRole"
}
]
}'
aws iam attach-role-policy \
--role-name lambda-container-execution \
--policy-arn arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSLambdaBasicE

AMD Publishes Open-Source GIM Driver For GPU Virtualization, Radeon "In The Roadmap"
Written by
Michael Larabel
in
AMD
on 23 April 2025 at 08:15 PM EDT.
31 Comments
AMD has published as open-source their "GPU-IOV Module" used for virtualization with Instinct accelerators. It's also reported on their roadmap for bringing virtualization support to their client (Radeon) discrete GPUs.
The AMD GPU-IOV Module is for the Linux kernel and for providing SR-IOV based hardware virtualization in conjunction with the KVM hypervisor. GIM provides the GPU IOV virtualization, virtual function (VF) configuration and enablement, GPU scheduling for world switch, hang detection and FLR reset, and PF/VF handshake capabilities.
Initially the AMD GIM driver is for the Instinct MI300X hardware and tested atop Ubuntu 22.04 LTS with ROCm 6.4. Those interested can find the AMD GIM code currently via
GitHub
. It's not laid out in the repository or any other public communications I've seen what any upstreaming plans are for this GIM driver to get it into the mainline Linux kernel.
Of interest to many Phoronix readers will be that GIM / SR-IOV support could be coming to client discrete GPUs, which has been a long sought feature for the Radeon graphics cards. AMD engineer Anush Elangovan responded on
X
that the client GPU support is reportedly "in the roadmap":
Hopefully this client GPU support pans out and comes sooner rather than later.
31 Comments

data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者如何使用Obsidian写作并快速发布博客。作者通过Obsidian进行本地纯文本写作，使用Hugo生成网站，并通过GitHub和Cloudflare Pages进行部署。具体步骤包括：安装Hugo并设置博客主题，将Obsidian与Hugo的文件夹结构连接，配置前置资料模板，本地预览文章，连接GitHub进行版本控制，以及使用Cloudflare Pages自动部署。整个流程初始设置较复杂，但完成后发布过程非常简便，只需写作、修改草稿状态、提交并推送到GitHub，Cloudflare会自动重建站点。这种方法提供了完全的控制权，无需订阅或担心平台变动。

43771645.article_content:
How I write my blogs in Obsidian and publish instantly
23 Apr, 2025
I’ve been using Obsidian for all my writing lately, and it’s been a game changer. The local-first model means everything lives as plain text on my machine, and with the Minimal theme, the interface stays clean and distraction-free.
My vault lives in iCloud (Dropbox or Google Drive work too), so notes sync seamlessly across devices - I often start drafts on my phone and finish them later on my laptop.
For publishing, I use Hugo with the Bear Blog theme (fast, minimal), and deploy via GitHub and Cloudflare Pages. This stack gives me full control: no subscriptions, no vendor lock-in, and no risk of platforms disappearing or changing policies.
If you:
Use (or want to try) Obsidian
Don’t mind a bit of technical setup
Prefer writing in plain text with Git-based version control
Want a fast, cost-free, portable publishing flow
Then this setup might be exactly what you’re looking for. Once set up, publishing is as simple as toggling a draft flag and pushing to GitHub.
Setting Up Your System
This post is a
high-level outline
of how it all fits together. It’s not a tutorial, but if you’re familiar with basic dev tools, it should be easy to follow. And if anything’s unclear, LLMs like ChatGPT or Claude are great for filling in the gaps.
1. Install and Set Up Hugo
First, you’ll need to
install Hugo
on your machine. Once installed, create a new site:
hugo new site myblog
cd myblog
Then add the Bear Blog theme (or your preferred theme):
git init
git submodule add https://github.com/janraasch/hugo-bearblog.git themes/hugo-bearblog
Update your
config.toml
file to use the theme. See the
Bear Blog theme documentation
for configuration options.
2. Connect Obsidian to Hugo
This is the key part. Hugo has a specific folder structure, and you want to write your posts in the
content
folder. Inside that folder, I created a
blog
subfolder for all my posts.
So my folder structure looks like this:
myblog/
├── content/
│   ├── blog/   <- This is where I write my posts
│   └── ...
└── ...
To set up Obsidian:
Open Obsidian
Click “Open folder as vault”
Navigate to your Hugo site’s blog folder (myblog/content/blog)
Select this folder
This way, everything you write in Obsidian goes directly into the right folder for Hugo to process.
3. Set Up Front Matter Template
In Obsidian, make sure that your posts includes the necessary Hugo front matter:
+++
title= "Your Post Title"
date= YYYY-MM-DD
tags= ["post"]
draft= true
+++
The
draft: true
tag is crucial - this is what you’ll toggle to
false
when you’re ready to publish.
4. Preview Posts Locally
While writing, I use Hugo’s local server with draft visibility:
hugo server -D
This lets me see how everything looks in-browser before pushing live.
5. Connect to GitHub
Create a new GitHub repository for your blog, then connect your local Hugo site:
git remote add origin https://github.com/yourusername/yourblog.git
git add .
git commit -m "Initial commit"
git push -u origin main
There are plenty of
GitHub tutorials
if you need help with this step.
6. Set Up Cloudflare Pages
Sign up for a
Cloudflare account
if you don’t have one
Go to the Pages section and create a new project
Connect to your GitHub account and select your blog repository
For build settings:
Build command:
hugo --minify
Build output directory:
public
Cloudflare’s
own documentation
covers this process well.
The Publishing Workflow
Once everything is set up, publishing is simple:
Write your post in Obsidian
When ready to publish, change
draft: true
to
draft: false
in the front matter
Commit and push to GitHub:
git add .
git commit -m "Publish new post"
git push
Cloudflare Pages will automatically detect the change and rebuild your site, typically within a minute or two.
Final Thoughts
This setup takes a bit of initial work, but the payoff is enormous. Once it’s all set up, this workflow fades into the background - I just write, commit, and publish. No friction, no fees, and everything stays in my hands. If you’re looking for a lightweight, sustainable way to blog, this might be worth trying.

data.author: wglb
data.article_summary: Cedars-Sinai研究人员开发了一种新型营养配方mBiota Elemental，用于治疗小肠细菌过度生长（SIBO）和肠道产甲烷菌过度生长（IMO）。这种可口元素饮食（PED）在临床试验中显示，多数患者的呼吸测试恢复正常，症状得到缓解，且无严重不良事件。试验为期两周，随后进行两周的正常饮食重新引入。结果显示，73%的患者呼吸测试正常，83%的患者症状明显缓解。此外，呼出甲烷和氢气水平显著下降，关键肠道微生物群的相对丰度减少。研究表明，mBiota Elemental作为一种非抗生素疗法，短期内对SIBO和IMO有效，且安全性高，副作用轻微。

- 元素饮食的实际效果和个体差异：有些人如Aurornis和部分研究数据支持其效果，而rikkert则以个人失败经验质疑其普适性。

- 成本与性价比：与其他饮食方式相比，元素饮食的费用较高，用户对此表示关注。

Clinical trial finds novel nutritional formula effectively treats gut microbial overgrowth
by Justin Jackson                                                                                , Medical Xpress
Credit: CC0 Public Domain
Cedars-Sinai researchers have developed a novel nutritional formula, mBiota Elemental, a palatable elemental diet (PED) that reduces the abundance of key gut microbiome taxa and improves symptoms in patients with small intestinal bacterial overgrowth (SIBO) and intestinal methanogen overgrowth (IMO).
Intervention testing with mBiota Elemental showed normalized breath tests and relief of symptoms in the majority of participants, with no serious or severe adverse events.
Elemental diets are highly digestible nutritional formulas containing free amino acids, simple carbohydrates, minimal fat, and essential micronutrients. Designed to provide complete nutrition with minimal stimulation of the digestive system, elemental diets have been used in conditions such as Crohn's disease, eosinophilic esophagitis/gastroenteritis, and chronic pancreatitis.
Intestinal microbial overgrowth syndromes, including SIBO and IMO, involve abnormally high levels of coliform bacteria or methanogenic archaea in the gastrointestinal tract. Antibiotics remain the primary treatment, yet normalization occurs in only about half of SIBO cases and fewer in IMO. Recurrence is common, often requiring repeated antibiotic courses which can have
deleterious effects
on the overall microbiome.
Previous retrospective findings suggested that elemental diets might reduce microbial overgrowth, yet no prospective clinical trials had tested this in patients with SIBO or IMO. Use of elemental diets in practice has been limited by poor palatability, which affects adherence in both pediatric and adult populations.
In the study, "Effect, tolerability, and safety of exclusive palatable elemental diet in patients with intestinal microbial overgrowth,"
published
in
Clinical Gastroenterology and Hepatology
, researchers conducted a prospective, open-label clinical trial to assess the effect, tolerability, and safety of a novel PED in adult subjects with SIBO and/or IMO.
A total of 30 adults with confirmed diagnoses of SIBO, IMO, or both based on lactulose breath tests were enrolled. All participants received a two-week course of mBiota Elemental PED, followed by a two-week period of regular food reintroduction.
Researchers used structured symptom questionnaires, daily visual analog scale ratings, stool image analysis through
artificial intelligence
, breath gas measurements, 16S rRNA gene sequencing of stool samples, and digital PCR analysis for Methanobrevibacter smithii. Body composition was measured with bioelectrical impedance, and blood tests were used to monitor electrolytes and glucose.
All 30 participants completed the two-week trial of mBiota Elemental. Breath test normalization occurred in 73% of subjects. Adequate global relief of symptoms was reported by 83%.
Significant reductions in exhaled methane and hydrogen levels were recorded, with average maximum methane decreasing from 41 to 12 parts per million (ppm) and hydrogen from 43 to 12 ppm. Fasting daily methane levels in subjects with IMO or IMO/SIBO dropped below 5 ppm by day five of the intervention.
Stool microbiome analysis revealed reduced relative abundance of key microbial groups, including Prevotella_9 and Fusobacterium, by the end of the trial. Digital PCR analysis showed that 92% of subjects with detectable
Methanobrevibacter smithii at baseline had reduced or undetectable levels by the end of the trial. Post‑PED, hydrogen production shifted from an early (small‑bowel) peak to a later (colonic) rise, indicating altered fermentation geography in the gut.
Symptom tracking showed significant improvements during the PED phase in bloating, distention, abdominal discomfort, constipation, and flatulence. Additional symptoms, including abdominal pain, fatigue, diarrhea, urgency, and brain fog, improved during the food reintroduction phase. Fasting electrolytes (sodium, potassium, chloride, bicarbonate) and glucose stayed within normal ranges throughout, addressing a common safety concern for elemental diets.
No serious or severe adverse events were reported. Mild side effects included diarrhea, cramps, nausea, fatigue, heartburn, belching, urgency, and transient hemorrhoidal bleeding. Subjects lost approximately 3 kg, driven mainly by reductions in total body fat and visceral fat.
Findings suggest a short-term course of mBiota Elemental may offer an effective non-antibiotic dietary approach for managing SIBO and IMO.

data.title: Show HN: I built an AI that turns GitHub codebases into easy tutorials
data.author: zh2408
data.article_summary: "Tutorial-Codebase-Knowledge" 是一个利用AI将代码库转化为新手教程的项目。该项目通过爬取GitHub仓库，分析代码核心结构并生成易于理解的教程，包含可视化说明。它使用Pocket Flow框架，一个100行的LLM（大语言模型）框架，自动生成针对流行GitHub仓库的AI教程。用户可以通过指定GitHub仓库或本地目录生成教程，支持多种语言输出（默认英文，可选中文）。项目提供了详细的入门指南和使用示例，包括设置LLM、安装依赖和运行主脚本进行代码分析与教程生成。该项目旨在帮助开发者快速理解陌生代码库。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI生成文档的质量、适用性及其在不同场景下的优缺点

不同观点：
• **bilalq**：认为生成的文档对于软件工程师来说过于基础，解释过于详尽且依赖过多类比，适合稍微懂技术的项目经理，而非开发人员。建议通过优化提示词来改善问题，并增加图表种类。
• **swashbuck1r**：关注AI生成文档在设计文档和代码生成中的应用，认为其展示了PocketFlow框架的实用性，并能有效地将文档设计转化为可运行的代码，对整个项目表示赞赏。
• **mooreds**：分享了使用不同代码库的体验，认为文档总体质量不错，但存在过度依赖类比的问题，且某些内容与具体应用无关。总体上对项目的质量表示肯定。
• **manofmanysmiles**：对项目持积极态度，但希望文档的语调能有所不同，建议增加“风格模板”以适应不同用户的偏好。
• **TheTaytay**：认为该项目能大大简化新库的上手步骤，表示赞赏。
• **iamsaitam**：批评项目过于冗长，认为文档和视频的长度不必要，强调质量不等于数量，建议减少不必要的文字。
• **Too**：质疑AI生成文档在未知代码库上的适用性，认为生成的内容过于具体且可能使用了外部训练数据，担心其准确性和原创性。
• **fforflo**：分享了使用Ollama运行本地模型的示例，并对使用不同模型（如GEMINI）生成文档的效果表示肯定。
• **chairhairair**：提到类似项目（mutable ai）曾被Google收购，指出其输出为wiki而非教程。
• **gregpr07**：表示对项目结果印象深刻，并考虑使用PocketFlow来解决文档维护问题。
• **remoquete**：认为AI生成的文档可以提供快速参考，但不能替代人工编写的文档，提供了一个外部链接以支持其观点。
• **esjeon**：认为高层次内容不错，但低层次内容像“用人类语言写的代码”，建议通过分析单元测试提取更有用的使用模式。
• **mattfrommars**：对项目能在一下午建成表示惊讶和赞赏，希望能学习到这种能力。
• **amelius**：提到曾建议使用LLM生成文档但遭到反对，对项目的实现表示赞赏。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于AI生成文档的质量和适用性，部分用户认为内容过于冗长或基础，而另一些用户则对其效率和实用性表示赞赏。
• 讨论中还涉及了如何通过优化提示词和图表种类来改善文档质量，以及AI生成文档在未知代码库上的表现。
• 一些用户分享了使用不同模型和工具生成文档的实际案例和经验。

data.title: Pixel is a unit of length and area
data.author: anitil
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：像素是否可以作为计量单位，以及其在不同上下文中的含义和使用方式

不同观点：
• Laremere认为，像素是一种计数单位，类似于用物体的数量来描述长度或面积。他举例说明，可以用苹果的数量来描述一个箱子的尺寸，类似地，像素也可以这样使用。这种用法是语言的简化表达，在不清楚的上下文中需要额外的说明来澄清。

• RedNifre指出，像素是图像元素，用作长度单位是口语化的用法，类似于用“车的长度”来描述距离。他建议使用Android的“dp”概念作为长度单位，以避免混淆。

• blenderob强烈反对将像素视为米一样的单位，认为像素是离散的对象，像点或苹果一样，不能用“平方米”的方式来处理。他强调像素作为离散单位的性质，并通过例子说明。

• otikik认为像素是物理事物，类似于瓷砖，可以用数量来描述，而不涉及任何复杂的单位转换或面积计算。

• jefftk认为像素的使用方式与其他矩形单位在日常语言中的使用一致，比如城市街区或瓷砖，都是通过数量来描述面积。

• ChrisMarshallNY指出像素的大小和形状是依赖于具体实现的，像素可以是点，也可以是非方形的，因此不能一概而论地将像素视为某种固定单位。

• dusted强调像素是二维实体，具有宽度和高度，不同于一维的米。他认为像素更像是物品，而不是纯粹的数学单位。

• ivan_gammel认为像素是无量纲单位，用于计数而不是测量，其形状和内部结构无关紧要。

• Sharlin认为像素作为分辨率单位，隐含了另一轴的分辨率，因此在某种程度上可以视为面积的度量单位，但实际上是无量纲的量。

补充讨论：
• 引用Alvy Ray Smith的论文《A Pixel Is Not a Little Square》来支持像素是点样本的观点，并批评将像素视为小方块的误解。

• 讨论中提到像素在不同设备上的实现差异，以及市场营销中使用像素和子像素作为卖点的现象。

• 提到科学家和工程师在处理单位时的不严谨和常见错误，反映了日常语言中单位使用的复杂性和不规范性。

争议焦点：
• 像素是否可以作为长度或面积的度量单位，以及在不同上下文中如何正确理解和使用像素这一概念。
• 像素作为离散对象与连续度量单位之间的本质区别，以及如何在实际应用中正确处理像素的数量和面积关系。

data.title: Differential Coverage for Debugging
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: Russ Cox介绍了一种称为“差异覆盖率”（Differential Coverage）的调试技术，用于比较通过测试和失败测试的代码覆盖率，以定位可能的错误代码。具体步骤包括：首先分别运行通过和失败的测试以生成覆盖率文件，然后通过`diff`命令比较这些文件，生成仅包含失败测试独特覆盖信息的文件，最后使用工具查看差异覆盖率，重点关注失败测试中执行但通过测试未执行的代码（绿色部分），从而快速锁定问题代码。该方法简单有效，但并非万无一失，某些情况下仍需结合其他调试手段。此外，单个失败测试的基本覆盖率信息也可帮助确定未执行的代码并非问题所在。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI生成代码的调试问题及相关工具和技术

不同观点：
• anougaret认为，随着AI生成代码的增加，调试“你没写过且不了解其逻辑流和数据流的代码”的问题会越来越严重。为此，他开发了Ariana工具，可以在IDE中查看哪些代码行被执行以及变量的值，无需手动添加日志或断点。Ariana还可以将生成的跟踪信息提供给大语言模型（LLM），让其自动解释代码行为并找到错误的根本原因。

• Jtsummers提供了一种相关的方法，提到通过收集多次测试运行数据，识别与失败运行最常关联的代码行。虽然这种方法不如直接对比通过和失败测试的覆盖报告那么简单，但仍然是一种有效的调试技术，并提供了一个相关的链接（Statistical Debugger）。

• drewcoo表示之前不知道这种调试方法有专门的名称，认为覆盖率差异（coverage diffs）是解决该问题的关键。他指出，困难在于那些偶尔失败且产生相同覆盖结果的测试，问题往往不在被测试的代码本身，常见的处理方式是重新运行测试或添加延迟来暂时解决问题。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中提到了几种调试工具和技术，包括Ariana和Statistical Debugger，展示了不同的调试策略和工具在处理复杂调试问题时的应用。
• 争议的焦点似乎在于如何有效地调试AI生成代码，特别是在缺乏对代码的直观理解和逻辑流、数据流信息的情况下，如何利用工具和技术来提高调试效率。
• 讨论还涉及了测试偶尔失败的问题，这增加了调试的复杂性，因为问题可能不在代码本身，而在测试环境或时间等外部因素。

43795090.article_content:
research!rsc
Thoughts and links about programming,
by
Russ Cox
RSS
Differential Coverage for Debugging
Posted on Friday, April 25, 2025.
I have been debugging some code I did not write and was reminded of this technique.
I’m sure it’s a very old debugging technique (like
bisection
),
but it should be more widely known.
Suppose you have one test case that’s failing.
You can get a sense of what code might be involved by comparing the code coverage
of successful tests with the code coverage of the failing test.
For example, I’ve inserted a bug into my development copy of
math/big
:
$
go test
--- FAIL: TestAddSub (0.00s)
int_test.go:2020: addSub(-0xffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff, 0xffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff) = -0x0, -0x1fffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffe, want 0x0, -0x1fffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffe
FAIL
exit status 1
FAIL	math/big	7.528s
$
Let’s collect a passing and failing profile:
$
go test -coverprofile=c1.prof -skip='TestAddSub$'
PASS
coverage: 85.0% of statements
ok  	math/big	8.373s
%
go test -coverprofile=c2.prof -run='TestAddSub$'
--- FAIL: TestAddSub (0.00s)
int_test.go:2020: addSub(-0xffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff, 0xffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff) = -0x0, -0x1fffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffe, want 0x0, -0x1fffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffe
FAIL
coverage: 4.7% of statements
exit status 1
FAIL	math/big	0.789s
$
Now we can diff them to make a profile showing what’s unique about the failing test:
$
(head -1 c1.prof; diff c[12].prof | sed -n 's/^> //p') >c3.prof
$
go tool cover -html=c3.prof
The
head -1
is preserving the one-line coverage profile header. The
diff | sed
saves only the lines unique to the failing test’s profile, and the
go tool cover -html
opens the profile in a web browser.
In the resulting profile, “covered” (green) means it ran in the failing test but not the passing ones, making it something to take a closer look at.
Looking at the file list, only
natmul.go
has a non-zero coverage percentage, meaning it contains lines that are unique to the failing test.
If we open
natmul.go
, we can see various lines in red (“uncovered”).
These lines ran in passing tests but not in the failing test. They are exonerated, although the fact that the lines normally run but were skipped in the failing test may prompt useful questions about what logic led to them being skipped. In this case, it’s just that the test does not exercise them: the
nat.mul
method has not been called at all.
Scrolling down, we find the one section of green.
This code is where I inserted the bug: the
else
branch is missing
za.neg = false
, producing the
-0x0
in the test failure.
Differential coverage is cheap to compute and display, and when it’s right, it can save a lot of time.
Out of over 15,000 lines of code, differential coverage identified 10, including the two relevant ones.
Of course, this technique is not foolproof: a passing test can still execute buggy code if the
bug is data-dependent, or if the test is not sensitive to the specific mistake in the code.
But a lot of the time, buggy code only triggers failures.
In those cases, differential coverage pinpoints the code blocks that merit a closer look.
You can
see the full profile here
.
A simpler but still useful technique is to view the basic coverage profile for a single failing test.
That gives you an accurate picture of which sections of code ran in the test, which can guide your
debugging: code that didn’t run is not the problem.
And if you are confused about how exactly a particular function returned an error,
the coverage pinpoints the exact error line.
In the example above, the failing test covered only 4.7% of the code.
Differential coverage also works for passing tests. Want to find the
code that implements the SOCK5 proxy in net/http
?
$
go test -short -skip=SOCKS5 -coverprofile=c1.prof net/http
$
go test -short -run=SOCKS5 -coverprofile=c2.prof net/http
$
(head -1 c1.prof; diff c[12].prof | sed -n 's/^> //p') >c3.prof
$
go tool cover -html=c3.prof
Have fun!

The role focuses on designing and developing advanced character animation systems in Unity, emphasizing performance on mobile devices. Responsibilities include building robust animation logic, integrating Inverse Kinematics (IK) systems, optimizing performance, and collaborating with artists and engineers. The ideal candidate has 6+ years of experience, deep Unity and C# expertise, and a proven track record in animation systems, especially for mobile games. Salary ranges from $160K to $250K with equity and benefits. The company, backed by top investors, aims to expand its game into new categories and platforms.

About the role
Role Summary
Gym Class is a leading social game on Meta Quest with millions of downloads, 71K ratings, and 4.9 stars. We’re now expanding the game to new interests and platforms, and looking for a talented and experienced Animation Engineer to drive the future of character movement and interaction in our evolving game world.
In this pivotal role, you'll take ownership of our animation systems built in Unity, focusing on delivering high-quality, performant, and engaging experiences, particularly for mobile and VR platforms. You'll work at the intersection of character motion, gameplay, and cutting-edge technology, collaborating closely with our co-founders, engineers, artists, and designers. If you're passionate about building robust and performant animation systems, leading a critical area of development, and shipping to an engaged community, we want to hear from you.
WHAT YOU'LL DO
Lead the design, development, and implementation of advanced character animation systems in Unity, with a strong emphasis on mobile performance.
Architect and build robust animation logic, including state machines, animation blending, and integration with Inverse Kinematics (IK) systems.
Develop solutions for seamless transitions between animation clips and IK, ensuring realistic and responsive character movement.
Implement collision detection and interaction support within the animation framework.
Optimize animation systems for performance on mobile devices, addressing memory usage, CPU/GPU impact, and ensuring smooth frame rates.
Collaborate closely with artists to understand their needs and build intuitive animation pipelines and tools within Unity.
Take ownership of the animation gameplay roadmap, contributing to the overall vision of character movement and expression.
Work closely with gameplay and AI engineers to integrate animation systems with other game mechanics.
Build and lead a high-performing animation engineering team as the roadmap and team scale.
QUALIFICATIONS
Deep Unity and C# Expertise
: Demonstrated proficiency in C# programming within the Unity engine, with 5+ years of professional experience building and shipping games.
Animation Engineering Focus
: Proven track record of designing, developing, and shipping animation systems and animation pipelines for games, ideally with experience on mobile platforms.
IK and Blending Mastery
: Strong understanding and practical experience with implementing and integrating Inverse Kinematics (IK) systems with animation clips in Unity. Expertise in blending animations effectively between different clips and with IK.
Animation State Machines
: Solid understanding of and experience implementing and managing character animation state machines within Unity's Animator Controller.
Mobile Performance Optimization:

data.title: Curry: A functional logic programming language
data.author: hyperbrainer
data.article_summary: Curry是一种集成函数式和逻辑式编程的语言，结合了函数式编程的特点（如嵌套表达式、高阶函数、强类型、惰性求值）和逻辑式编程的特点（如非确定性、内置搜索、自由变量、部分数据结构）。它支持纯声明式编程、类型推断、非确定性操作和自由变量等特性。Curry的开发是一个国际项目，提供了一个用于研究、教学和应用集成函数逻辑语言的平台。Curry有多种实现，如PAKCS、KiCS2和MCC。Curry还拥有自己的包管理器CPM、文档生成工具CurryDoc和API搜索引擎Curr(y)gle。

不同观点：
• [taeric] 认为示例不容易理解，可能是因为不熟悉其风格。这表明对新语言或特定编程范式的入门难度存在困惑。

• [abathologist] 提出Curry（具有Haskell-like语法并支持Prolog特性）与Mercury（具有Prolog-like语法并支持Haskell特性）的比较问题，关注两种语言的语法和特性差异。

• [badmonster] 关注Curry如何处理非确定性计算中的多重有效实例化问题，尤其是自由变量的处理，这是对语言处理复杂计算能力的疑问。

• [currando] 提供Curry的学习资源，并提及一个相关讨论线程，表明对Curry文档和社区资源的认可，同时也引出对具体讨论内容的兴趣。

• [pmarreck] 表达了对新语言的常见需求，希望看到Curry与其他语言在速度、代码示例、依赖性、特性（如不可变数据、静态类型等）方面的比较，这是对具体技术细节和实用性的关注。

• [johnnyjeans] 对逻辑语言的比较持怀疑态度，认为将非确定性作为逻辑编程的特性是不寻常的，并强调Prolog及其Horn子句语法的独特性和价值。对Curry及其他类似语言持悲观态度，认为静态类型和Horn子句的结合并不理想，同时呼吁逻辑编程系统架构的进一步发展。

补充讨论：
• [otherayden] 以幽默的方式评论了名字与编程语言的关系，未涉及技术讨论。

• [Zambyte] 提供相关链接，包括Haskell和Haskell Curry的维基百科页面，为讨论提供背景信息。

争议焦点：
• Curry和Mercury的比较，以及它们各自的语法和特性优劣。
• 逻辑编程语言中非确定性和Horn子句的处理方式及其价值。
• Prolog及其衍生语言在语法和执行模型上的独特性及其优劣对比。

Curry is a
declarative multi-paradigm programming language
which combines in a seamless way features from
functional programming
(nested expressions, higher-order functions, strong typing, lazy evaluation)
and
logic programming
(non-determinism, built-in search, free variables, partial data structures).
Compared to the single programming paradigms, Curry provides
additional features, like optimal evaluation for logic-oriented
computations and flexible, non-deterministic pattern matching
with user-defined functions.
Features
Purely Declarative
Curry is called a declarative language, because computed results are independent of the time and order of evaluation, which simplifies reasoning on programs. Side effects can be modeled as âIOâ operations, i.e., a declarative description of what to do. Operations are constructed by expressions only, there are no statements or instructions, and every binding to a variable is immutable.
Learn More
Type Inference
Curry is strongly typed but type annotations of functions need not be written by the programmer: they are automatically inferred by the compiler using a type inference algorithm. Nevertheless, it is a good style to write down the types of functions in order to provide at least a minimal documentation of the intended use of functions.
Learn More
Non-Determinism
Curry supports non-deterministic operations which can return different values for the same input. Non-deterministic operations support a programming style similar to that of logic programming while preserving some advantages of functional programs such as expression nesting and lazy (demand-driven) evaluation.
Learn More
Free Variables
Free variables denote âunknownâ values. They are instantiated (i.e., replaced by some concrete values) so that the instantiated expression is evaluable. REPLs of Curry systems show bindings (i.e., instantiations) of the free variables of the main expression it has computed to evaluate an expression.
Learn More
The development of Curry is an international
initiative intended to provide a common platform for the research, teaching and application of integrated
functional logic languages. The design of Curry is mainly discussed in the Curry mailing list. A detailed report
describing the language is also available. To get an idea of Curry, you may have a look into the short list of
Curry's features or a tutorial on Curry.
Curry Report
Features
Tutorial
Mailing List
Ecosystem
Compilers
Several implementations of Curry are available and/or under development. The most prominent representatives are the Portland Aachen Kiel Curry System (PAKCS), the new version of the Kiel Curry System (KiCS2), and the MÃ¼nster Curry Compiler (MCC).
Learn More
Package Manager
The Curry Package Manager (CPM) is a tool to distribute and install Curry libraries and applications and manage version dependencies between them. These libraries are organized in packages. There is a central index of all these packages which can easily be downloaded by CPM.
Learn More
CurryDoc
CurryDoc is a tool that generates the documentation for a Curry program in HTML (and optionally also LaTeX) format. The generated HTML pages contain information about all data types and operations exported by a module as well as links between the different entities.
Learn More
Curr(y)gle API Search
Curr(y)gle is a Curry API search engine which allows you to search the Curry libraries indexed by CPM. You can search by names of either operations, data types, and modules. It was designed following the example set by Haskellâs search engine Hoogle.
Learn More

data.title: Show HN: Formalizing Principia Mathematica using Lean
data.author: ndrwnaguib
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了作者使用Lean定理证明助手重新形式化伯特兰·罗素《数学原理》第一卷的工作。目标是确保形式化内容与原书定理一致，避免混淆。作者提到《数学原理》的符号非常复杂，但通过一些例子和对比，读者应能理解其形式化过程。作者尽量严格遵循罗素的证明，仅在必要时添加少量语句。项目中包含每个定理的LaTeX片段，并推荐使用Emacs或VSCode的扩展来增强阅读体验。文章还详细介绍了如何在Lean中实现罗素的某些推理过程，特别是通过元编程创建新战术以遵循其符号。尽管已有使用Coq的形式化工作，作者认为用Lean4实现同样有趣。

Formalizing Bertrand Russell’s Principia Mathematica Using Lean4
This
project
aims to formalize the first volume of Prof. Bertrand Russell’s
Principia Mathematica using the Lean theorem prover. The goal is to ensure that
the formalization aligns clearly with the corresponding theorems in the book to
avoid confusion (See
Metaprogramming =Syll=
)
Notation
Principia Mathematica
’s notation (Peano-Russell notation) is exceptionally known
for its sophistication that it
has a separate entry on the Stanford Encyclopedia
of Philosophy (SEP)
. Also, Prof. Landon Elkind’s
Squaring the Circles: a
Genealogy of Principia’s Dot Notation
explains the notation skillfully.
I do not think there is a
need
to read them, I would like to believe that
after reading a few examples of how some formulas were formalized and
contrasting them against Prof. Russell’s notation should make it clear.
Throughout the formalization, I tried to rigorously follow Prof. Russell’s
proof, with no or little added statements from my side, which were only
necessary for the formalization but not the logical argument. Should you notice
any inaccuracy (even if it does not necessarily falsify the proof), please let
me know as I would like to proceed with the same spirit of rigor as Prof.
Russell.
Before starting this project, I had already found
Prof. Elkind’s formalization
of the Principia using Coq
, which is much mature work than this one. However, I
still thought it would be fun to do it using Lean4 (See
Remarks
).
Editing
I have included a
$\LaTeX$
fragment with each theorem that represents Prof. Russell’s
proof. If you use Emacs, I recommend enabling
org-preview-latex
in the Lean
buffer. If you are using VSCode, perhaps a similar experience can be achieved by
installing the
Better Comments
extension. This is how it looked like for me:
Notes on the formalization
$∗ 1 ⋅ 11$
Prof. Russell repeatedly used *1.11 to indicate the inference of a proposition
from another, for example
$[(3).(8).∗ 1⋅ 11]$
is the proposition deduced by chaining
proposition (8) and (3). In Lean, this could be analogous to several tactics or
atoms, e.g.,
<|
,
simp
, etc.
Metaprogramming
Syll
The experience I planned for when reading the formalization is to have the
corresponding text in the Principia included in the same file, only with Prof.
Russell’s proofs replaced with their Lean formalization. For example, here is
*2.16 along with a unique part in the formalization, that is
metaprogramming a
new tactic
to follow Prof. Russell’s notation for
Syll
:

data.title: Lossless LLM compression for efficient GPU inference via dynamic-length float
data.author: CharlesW
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种名为Dynamic-Length Float (DFloat11) 的无损压缩框架，旨在减少大型语言模型（LLM）的存储大小（减少30%）的同时，保持模型输出的完全一致性。DFloat11通过熵编码根据权重频率分配动态长度编码，从而实现接近信息最优的压缩。为了实现高效的GPU推理，作者开发了自定义GPU内核，支持在线快速解压，并通过分解内存密集型查找表、协调线程读写位置以及按块解压等技术优化性能。实验表明，DFloat11在多款最新模型上实现了30%的模型大小缩减，且在生成任务中吞吐量提高了1.9-38.8倍。同时，在固定GPU内存预算下，支持的上下文长度增加了5.3-13.17倍。代码和模型已开源。

Authors:

View a PDF of the paper titled 70% Size, 100% Accuracy: Lossless LLM Compression for Efficient GPU Inference via Dynamic-Length Float, by Tianyi Zhang and 5 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Large Language Models (LLMs) have grown rapidly in size, creating significant challenges for efficient deployment on resource-constrained hardware. In this paper, we introduce Dynamic-Length Float (DFloat11), a lossless compression framework that reduces LLM size by 30% while preserving outputs that are bit-for-bit identical to the original model. DFloat11 is motivated by the low entropy in the BFloat16 weight representation of LLMs, which reveals significant inefficiency in existing storage format. By applying entropy coding, DFloat11 assigns dynamic-length encodings to weights based on frequency, achieving near information-optimal compression without any loss of precision. To facilitate efficient inference with dynamic-length encodings, we develop a custom GPU kernel for fast online decompression. Our design incorporates the following: (i) decomposition of memory-intensive lookup tables (LUTs) into compact LUTs that fit in GPU SRAM, (ii) a two-phase kernel for coordinating thread read/write positions using lightweight auxiliary variables, and (iii) transformer-block-level decompression to minimize latency. Experiments on recent models, including Llama-3.1, Qwen-2.5, and Gemma-3, validates our hypothesis that DFloat11 achieves around 30% model size reduction while preserving bit-for-bit exact outputs. Compared to a potential alternative of offloading parts of an uncompressed model to the CPU to meet memory constraints, DFloat11 achieves 1.9-38.8x higher throughput in token generation. With a fixed GPU memory budget, DFloat11 enables 5.3-13.17x longer context lengths than uncompressed models. Notably, our method enables lossless inference of Llama-3.1-405B, an 810GB model, on a single node equipped with 8x80GB GPUs. Our code and models are available at

data.title: Paper2Code: Automating Code Generation from Scientific Papers
data.author: Jerry2
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一种名为PaperCoder的框架，利用大型语言模型（LLM）将机器学习领域的学术论文自动转化为可运行的代码库。PaperCoder分为三个阶段：规划阶段生成高层次路线图和系统架构，分析阶段解读具体实现细节，生成阶段输出模块化且依赖感知的代码。该框架通过多个专门的代理模型协作完成各阶段任务，并在模型评估和人工评估中表现出色，尤其在PaperBench基准测试中超越了其他基准模型。实验结果验证了PaperCoder在生成高质量、忠实于原文的代码实现方面的有效性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：从论文自动生成代码的可行性与潜在问题

不同观点：
• [somethingsome] 认为自动从论文生成代码的想法有吸引力，但存在隐患。他担心这样会导致大量低质量、难以维护的代码充斥在GitHub上，使得不同论文的实现难以理解和修改。他还指出，通过阅读作者的代码可以学到很多细节，而这些细节可能在论文中被省略。此外，代码的可靠性也是一个问题，因为论文和实现之间并非一一对应的关系。

• [colkassad] 对自动生成代码持较为积极的态度，认为如果能将论文和其实现进行对比（如通过某些工具），将是一个很有用的功能。他分享了一个工具链接（Paper2Code），可能用于实现这一目的。

• [ks2048] 以调侃的语气提出是否存在一个从代码生成论文的模型，可以与自动生成代码的模型形成闭环，暗示对自动化学术写作的幽默看法。

Authors:

View a PDF of the paper titled Paper2Code: Automating Code Generation from Scientific Papers in Machine Learning, by Minju Seo and 3 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Despite the rapid growth of machine learning research, corresponding code implementations are often unavailable, making it slow and labor-intensive for researchers to reproduce results and build upon prior work. In the meantime, recent Large Language Models (LLMs) excel at understanding scientific documents and generating high-quality code. Inspired by this, we introduce PaperCoder, a multi-agent LLM framework that transforms machine learning papers into functional code repositories. PaperCoder operates in three stages: planning, where it constructs a high-level roadmap, designs the system architecture with diagrams, identifies file dependencies, and generates configuration files; analysis, which focuses on interpreting implementation-specific details; and generation, where modular, dependency-aware code is produced. Moreover, each phase is instantiated through a set of specialized agents designed to collaborate effectively across the pipeline. We then evaluate PaperCoder on generating code implementations from machine learning papers based on both model-based and human evaluations, specifically from the original paper authors, with author-released repositories as ground truth if available. Our results demonstrate the effectiveness of PaperCoder in creating high-quality, faithful implementations. Furthermore, it consistently shows strengths in the recently released PaperBench benchmark, surpassing strong baselines by substantial margins.

data.title: Done in by Time
data.author: lermontov
data.article_summary: 本文由Joseph Epstein撰写，探讨了艺术与时间的关系，指出艺术（包括文学、音乐、绘画和雕塑）的历史并非进步史，而是有高峰和低谷。当前艺术处于低潮期，尤其在文学领域，数字文化的兴起导致注意力缩短，出版商也不再青睐“文学小说”。Edwin Frank的《Stranger Than Fiction: Lives of the Twentieth-Century Novel》分析了20世纪小说的命运，这一世纪的巨变深刻影响了小说形式。书中讨论了32位小说家的作品，并提到若时间允许，还有71位作家也值得纳入。文章特别提及了陀思妥耶夫斯基的《地下室手记》作为20世纪小说的先驱，尽管其最初并未广受关注，但预示了后来的重要作品如《罪与罚》。
data.comments_summary:

Unlike science, the history of art is not a story of progress. Instead, art—all the arts: literature, music, painting, and sculpture—has high and low periods of varying lengths. Just now, for example, in the realm of high art, we are going through a low period. If you doubt this, ask yourself the work of which contemporary novelist, poet, composer, or painter you are eagerly awaiting. I’ll pause here a moment while you fail to find any.
Various reasons have been put forth to explain the current low state into which the arts have fallen. In literature, the dominance of digital culture is cited prominently among them: the computer, the tablet, the cell phone, all of which encourage a shortened attention span, a scroll-down outlook on life. Publishers have also been blamed. The big five American publishing conglomerates—Penguin Random House, Hachette, Macmillan, HarperCollins, and Simon & Schuster—are said no longer to be interested in publishing what goes by the name of “literary fiction” but is really serious fiction, finding it commercially too risky. Of late there even has been talk of novels being produced to a surefire commercial formula by artificial intelligence.
Then there are periods in which certain literary forms or modes dominate. In classical antiquity we had the epic, the drama, the satire. Drama dominated the Renaissance, and poetry came into its own early in the nineteenth century. “To become a poet of the first rank, great talent is not enough,” W. H. Auden declared. “One must also get born at the right time and in the right place.” He believed the right time was between 1870 and 1890, a period of great ferment in the arts generally. Auden was born in 1907. The nineteenth century was also the great age of the novel in Russia, England, and France.
In
Stranger Than Fiction: Lives of the Twentieth-Century Novel
, Edwin Frank, a man of wide literary learning who is the editorial director of New York Review Books and founder of the distinguished N.Y.R.B. Classics series, takes up the fate of the novel in the twentieth century. I say the “fate” because the destiny of books, like that of people, is subject to the conditions in which the books come into being. The twentieth century, with its world wars, its adamant ideologies, its mass murders, was more than tumultuous. It was, as Frank notes, “a century of staggering transformation.” The effect on the novel, that literary form whose subject, to cite the title of Anthony Trollope’s novel, is
The Way We Live Now
, could not be other than radical.
Stranger Than Fiction
is “the story of an exploding form in an exploding world.”
The book is also, as its author notes in his introduction, “an essay in literary history, a work of descriptive criticism.” In twenty-one chapters he takes up the work of thirty-two novelists. Among novelists who wrote important criticism of the novel, he is most taken with Henry James, Virginia Woolf, and D. H. Lawrence. He makes no claims for completeness, and at the close of his book, he lists seventy-one other writers and novels that, given world enough and time, he might also have included in his book.
Frank begins with a consideration of not a twentieth-century but a nineteenth-century novella, Fyodor Dostoevsky’s
Notes from
Underground.
He views this complex work, published in 1864, as a precursor of the turns the novel would take in the twentieth century. Part satire, part parody, the book luxuriates in paradox.
Notes from Underground
is narrated by a highly cultivated masochist, who suggests that perhaps his book was misgottten. “I believe I made a mistake in beginning to write this
story
,” he writes toward the book’s close, “so it’s hardly literature as much as corrective punishment.”
Notes from Underground
has neither a happy nor sad ending, or really any ending at all. In the Ralph E. Matlaw translation, it concludes, “The
‘
notes’ of this paradoxolist do not end here, however. He could not resist and continued them. But it also seems to me that we may stop here.”
Nor did the book meet with a wide readership at its original publication. In his splendid biography of Dostoevsky, Joseph Frank notes that “it is very likely that he considered the work a failure” and that he “never again attempted anything so hermetic and allusive as
Notes from
Underground.
” Yet in its pages Frank also sees an adumbrated

43797505.article_summary: 本文由Joseph Epstein撰写，探讨了艺术与时间的关系，指出艺术（包括文学、音乐、绘画和雕塑）的历史并非进步史，而是有高峰和低谷。当前艺术处于低潮期，尤其在文学领域，数字文化的兴起导致注意力缩短，出版商也不再青睐“文学小说”。Edwin Frank的《Stranger Than Fiction: Lives of the Twentieth-Century Novel》分析了20世纪小说的命运，这一世纪的巨变深刻影响了小说形式。书中讨论了32位小说家的作品，并提到若时间允许，还有71位作家也值得纳入。文章特别提及了陀思妥耶夫斯基的《地下室手记》作为20世纪小说的先驱，尽管其最初并未广受关注，但预示了后来的重要作品如《罪与罚》。

data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了加州南部沙漠地区传说中的神秘生物“Yucca Man”，其目击报告自20世纪60年代起常见于新闻和电视。这种生物被描述为类似大脚怪的毛茸茸怪物，常在Twentynine Palms军事基地和约书亚树国家公园等地出没，吓坏新兵和露营者。尽管一些业余研究者试图证明其存在，原住民则视其为超自然 entity，称之为“hairy devils”或“Takwis”，并避而远之。类似的怪物传说也在Fontana的赛车场和Antelope Valley的新郊区流传。文章还呼吁读者支持Longreads，以帮助维持优质新闻报道。

主要讨论点：Ken Layne的《Desert Oracle》广播节目及其相关内容引发的讨论，包括节目的特点、主题以及对奇异现象的看法。

不同观点：
• jjwiseman认为《Desert Oracle》广播节目是他的最爱，涵盖了沙漠生活、户外活动、UFO、神秘生物、真实犯罪等主题。他将该节目视为Art Bell（著名电台主持人，以讨论超自然现象闻名）的精神继承者，并提到还有一个《Desert Oracle》的纸质杂志。jjwiseman提供了更多信息的文章链接，供其他用户参考。

• swayvil提出了一个哲学性的观点，认为现实是由人类构建的。他指出，人类越集中的地方，事物越显得正常；而在荒野等人类稀少的地方，则会遇到怪异的事情。如果一个人本身就比较独特，那么在荒野中会更加契合。这一观点带有一种存在主义和环境影响现实的思考。

补充讨论：
• jjwiseman对《Desert Oracle》的积极评价和推荐，特别是将其与Art Bell比较，表明了该节目在超自然和神秘现象爱好者中的受欢迎程度。
• swayvil的观点引入了一种更为抽象的讨论，涉及到人类与环境、现实本质的关系，这为评论增加了一个哲学思考的层面。

总体来看，评论从对具体节目内容的欣赏转向了对现实和环境影响的深层次思考。

Desert Oracle
| Winter 2015 | 11 minutes (2,903 words)
The story you’ll hear most often goes like this: There’s a young Marine on guard duty in some far-off corner of the massive Twentynine Palms desert training base. He hears an awful sound in the dark, something like a growl. Then, the breathing, coming from one side of his lonesome little guard booth and now from the other.
It’s circling him.
He steps out into the dark, his sidearm drawn. There it stands, eight feet tall, an unbearable stench from its hairy body, the eyes glowing like red coals.
Sometimes, the Marine is knocked unconscious by the beast and found hours later by the next shift. One version occurs at the old rifle range, where the watchman — also armed with a rifle — wakes from the assault to find his weapon bent in half.
Since the 1970s, when the Mojave Desert base expanded from its World War II encampment, there have been regular reports of new recruits terrorized by both the Yucca Man and pranks inspired by the tales. But most sightings of the spectral creature come from campers and hikers at Joshua Tree National Park. Tents have been opened in the night by stinking monstrosities, and there is an occasional large footprint or blurry photograph submitted as evidence. A snapshot from the Hidden Valley campground has made the rounds for a decade now: The figure bounding over the boulders looks much like the iconic Bigfoot from the Patterson–Gimlin film of 1967.
A photograph of the alleged Yucca Man from the 1990s.
Since the 1960s, when tales of Yucca Man and his desert cohorts were commonly reported by Southern California newspapers and television stations, amateur “cryptozoologists” and Bigfoot researchers have analyzed the blurry pictures and measured the prints in the sand, all in the effort to document a flesh-and-blood creature they believe exists alongside everyday mammals such as bears, coyotes, and humans.
But the Natives who lived in California long before European colonization considered these creatures to be supernatural entities, with names that often translated to “hairy devils.” They took care to avoid the gloomy spots where the devils were often seen.
The Tongva People living around the Santa Ana River called the devils’ hideout east of the river’s source in the San Bernardino Mountains the Camp of the Takwis, pronounced the same as the
Tahquitz
known to the Cahuilla of Agua Caliente. According to John Reed Swanton’s
The Indian Tribes of North America,
“Takwis” also survives as a site name at the head of the Santa Margarita River, at Temecula Creek. Throughout Palm Springs and the Coachella Valley, you’ll see it spelled
Tahquitz
— the angry specter’s unhappy home in the region is the cursed Tahquitz Canyon.
Sometimes the Takwis or Tahquitz played a role in creation stories, as in Cahuilla culture. Other times the creature was an omen, or simply something weird in the wilderness that should be avoided. To the Cahuilla, the Tahquitz could be the “original shaman” and a murderous monstrosity that collected victims from Tahquitz Rock (or Lily Rock). “Tahquitz has also been said to manifest as a large green fireball moving through the night sky,” the website Weird California reports.

Sign up now
That coastal and desert Indians should know the same creature is not in itself cause for skepticism: Under various names and dressed in myriad traditions, Yucca Man has been reported in the wilder parts of Southern California as long as people have lived here.
In Fontana, that hard and wind-blown Inland Empire town, there was a famed racetrack north of Foothill Boulevard called Mickey Thompson’s Fontana Dragway. From 1955 to the dragway’s closure in 1972 following a gruesome series of fatal crashes, spectators repeatedly saw something they called the ‘Speedway Monster.’ Assumed to be a “wild man” resident of the foothills of the nearby San Bernardino Mountains, it had the habit of crossing the rural land at the dragway’s edge, during car races that produced horrific noise.

data.title: Programming in D: Tutorial and Reference
data.author: teleforce
data.article_summary: 《Programming in D》是一本全面介绍D编程语言的教程和参考书，涵盖了从基础语法到高级特性的广泛内容。书中详细讲解了D语言的各种数据类型、控制结构、函数、异常处理、模板、操作符重载、并发编程等主题。此外，还介绍了D语言的独特功能，如关联数组、契约编程、UFCS（通用函数调用语法）、混合编程等。该书提供了多种格式，包括纸质版、Kindle版、互动课程以及免费的电子书格式。对于希望深入了解D语言的开发者来说，这是一本详尽而实用的指南。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：D语言与其他编程语言的比较及其实用性

不同观点：
• [usrbinenv] 认为一些被广泛使用的编程语言（如Python、TypeScript、Go）虽然被普遍接受，但其实不如一些不太流行的语言（如Ruby、Dart、Crystal、D）优越。他指出，尽管后者生态系统不如前者丰富，但作为编程语言本身更优秀。他还批评了选择" inferior"技术的趋势。
• [zascrash] 赞同D语言的优越性，并希望有大型企业支持D语言，使其获得更多认可。他还表达了对D语言创建者Walter Bright的钦佩。
• [shoozza] 关注D语言是否适合用于创建极小的可执行文件，尤其是在游戏开发比赛（4mb jam 2025）中，是否能像C语言那样生成小于8KB的游戏提交。
• [WalterBright] 作为D语言的创建者，分享了其当前的工作进展，尤其是为D编译器添加AArch64代码生成器，并对技术挑战进行了评价。
• [Daunk] 和 [kingbob000] 都认为D语言被低估，虽然他们承认在当前的开发环境中很难找到使用D语言的理由。

补充讨论：
• [bachmeier] 分享了自己自2013年以来使用D语言的经验，并提到一本对其有帮助的书籍（或笔记）。
• [croemer] 提出了一个技术问题，即在macOS上使用LDC2编译的程序会崩溃，并提供了相关的GitHub问题链接。
• [nerdralph] 表示自己曾尝试使用D语言，但因为缺乏像Perl、Python、C++等语言那样丰富的库支持，最终没有继续使用。
• [acehreli] 作为作者，邀请大家向他提问（AMA）。
• [bsdooby] 称赞了D语言的参考手册，认为它是最好的语言参考手册之一。
• [jpecar] 提出了一个关于D语言运行时在多于128个CPU核心的主机上崩溃的技术问题。

争议焦点：
• D语言与其他语言相比的优越性及其在实际开发中的实用性。一些评论者认为D语言在技术上更优越，但缺乏生态系统支持，导致难以在实际项目中广泛使用。
• D语言在特定技术环境（如macOS、多核CPU）中的技术问题，显示出其实际使用中的一些局限性。

43798009.article_summary: 《Programming in D》是一本全面介绍D编程语言的教程和参考书，涵盖了从基础语法到高级特性的广泛内容。书中详细讲解了D语言的各种数据类型、控制结构、函数、异常处理、模板、操作符重载、并发编程等主题。此外，还介绍了D语言的独特功能，如关联数组、契约编程、UFCS（通用函数调用语法）、混合编程等。该书提供了多种格式，包括纸质版、Kindle版、互动课程以及免费的电子书格式。对于希望深入了解D语言的开发者来说，这是一本详尽而实用的指南。
43798009.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：D语言与其他编程语言的比较及其实用性

不同观点：
• [usrbinenv] 认为一些被广泛使用的编程语言（如Python、TypeScript、Go）虽然被普遍接受，但其实不如一些不太流行的语言（如Ruby、Dart、Crystal、D）优越。他指出，尽管后者生态系统不如前者丰富，但作为编程语言本身更优秀。他还批评了选择" inferior"技术的趋势。
• [zascrash] 赞同D语言的优越性，并希望有大型企业支持D语言，使其获得更多认可。他还表达了对D语言创建者Walter Bright的钦佩。
• [shoozza] 关注D语言是否适合用于创建极小的可执行文件，尤其是在游戏开发比赛（4mb jam 2025）中，是否能像C语言那样生成小于8KB的游戏提交。
• [WalterBright] 作为D语言的创建者，分享了其当前的工作进展，尤其是为D编译器添加AArch64代码生成器，并对技术挑战进行了评价。
• [Daunk] 和 [kingbob000] 都认为D语言被低估，虽然他们承认在当前的开发环境中很难找到使用D语言的理由。

补充讨论：
• [bachmeier] 分享了自己自2013年以来使用D语言的经验，并提到一本对其有帮助的书籍（或笔记）。
• [croemer] 提出了一个技术问题，即在macOS上使用LDC2编译的程序会崩溃，并提供了相关的GitHub问题链接。
• [nerdralph] 表示自己曾尝试使用D语言，但因为缺乏像Perl、Python、C++等语言那样丰富的库支持，最终没有继续使用。
• [acehreli] 作为作者，邀请大家向他提问（AMA）。
• [bsdooby] 称赞了D语言的参考手册，认为它是最好的语言参考手册之一。
• [jpecar] 提出了一个关于D语言运行时在多于128个CPU核心的主机上崩溃的技术问题。

争议焦点：
• D语言与其他语言相比的优越性及其在实际开发中的实用性。一些评论者认为D语言在技术上更优越，但缺乏生态系统支持，导致难以在实际项目中广泛使用。
• D语言在特定技术环境（如macOS、多核CPU）中的技术问题，显示出其实际使用中的一些局限性。

data.title: Echo – Open Hardware Music Player
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: Echo是一个开源硬件音乐播放器项目，旨在打造高质量音乐播放器，采用免费软件设计，主要运行Rockbox固件，支持多种音频格式和功能。硬件设计使用KiCAD 8.0，外壳计划用FreeCAD设计，所有设计遵循CERN-OHL-S v2许可证。当前版本为Echo R1，尺寸约为60x100x15毫米，配有4向D-pad和6个多功能按钮，具备专用音量和电源按钮，以及防止误触的锁定开关。它有两个3.5毫米插孔，支持同时使用，并可扩展至2 TiB存储。供电采用可更换的BL-5C电池，USB-C接口用于充电和文件传输。目前Rev1原型已完成，但存在一些问题，正在进行Rockbox移植和外壳设计，未来版本将解决这些问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对Sony新款Walkman类设备的评价和期望，涉及硬件设计、软件开放性、以及与其他开源硬件的对比。

不同观点：
• [vinceguidry] 希望设备能有一个clickwheel（点击滚轮），并猜测Sony使用的部件是内部制造的，同时对设备本身表示赞赏。
• [loughnane] 表达了对设备机械设计使用Onshape（一种云端CAD工具）的期望，认为这样更有利于协作，并表示愿意贡献设计。
• [JKCalhoun] 对设备的芯片组信息感兴趣，但表示不愿自己下载KiCAD文件去查找。
• [teruakohatu] 长期以来希望有类似设备，并建议可以改装为使用更常见的18650电池，而不是较为少见的BL-5C电池。
• [ashafq] 对设备表示喜爱，并提到自己曾是Rockbox（开源音乐播放器固件）的粉丝。
• [stonogo] 提供了另一个开源硬件音乐播放器Tangara的链接，指出其与Echo R1的区别，包括I/O接口的不同（普通耳机插孔与TRRS插孔及线路输出插孔）。
• [mouse_] 对设备能运行Rockbox表示强烈支持。
• [rkagerer] 原本期待是亚马逊Echo的开源固件，对标题有些误解。

补充讨论：
• 用户对设备开放性的关注，尤其是对Rockbox的支持和期望。
• 用户对硬件改装的兴趣，特别是电池类型的更换，以提高设备的可用性和便利性。
• 不同开源硬件设备之间的比较，如Tangara和Echo R1，在功能和设计上的区别。
• 对设备设计工具和文件开放性的期望，以便于社区协作和改进。

争议焦点：
• 设备是否开放以及开放的程度，特别是机械设计文件和固件的开放性，是部分用户关注的焦点。

Echo: Open Hardware Music Player
Echo is an open hardware platform for music players. The goal of
the project is to produce a high quality music player, based on
and designed with free software. It's primarily designed to run
Rockbox
, a free music player firmware
with support for many codecs, and a wide array of features.
KiCAD 8.0 was used for the electrical design and PCB layout.
The planned 3D-printable case will be designed using FreeCAD.
The designs themselves are available under the CERN-OHL-S v2
license.
The current version of the Echo player is called the Echo R1.
In the future, there could be new player models if there are
significant changes to the features or form factor, but old
models will always be supported.
Echo R1
Size: 60x100x15mm (approx)
Weight: TBD
The R1 has a 4-way D-pad and 6 multi-function buttons on the
faceplate, which can be used to quickly navigate your music
library and control playback. There are dedicated volume and
power buttons (not pictured), and a sliding hold switch near
the power button, which locks the buttons against accidental
presses when the player is in your pocket or bag.
There are two 3.5mm jacks, one for headphones, and one true
line-out port. The headphone jack supports recording from an
in-line microphone and playback control by an in-line remote.
Both jacks can be used simultaneously.
The removable memory card slot allows up to 2 TiB of storage
for your music and files. The USB-C port is used for charging
and file transfer, and supports high-speed USB 2.0.
The battery socket accepts the widely available BL-5C battery,
and the battery can easily be replaced without special tools
when it starts to wear out.
Hardware specifications
Component
Description
CPU
STM32H743 @ 480 MHz
Memory
32 MiB SDRAM @ 120 MHz
Audio
TLV320AIC3104, up to 96 KHz, 0.707 V RMS
Display
18-bit, 320x240, 2.3 inch LCD
Storage
Expandable external memory card slot
USB
USB 2.0 @ 480 Mbps (High-speed)
Headphone out
Yes (3.5mm jack)
Line out
Yes (3.5mm jack)
Microphone
Can use wired headphone mic
RTC
Yes, with wake-up alarm function
Battery
Replaceable BL-5C battery (~1000 mAH)
Status
The Rev1 prototype PCB is complete but has some problems (see the
list of known issues below). A 3D-printable case for the Rev1 is
planned, but CAD files aren't available yet.
Development is currently focused on two areas:
Porting Rockbox to the Rev1 board to identify any issues with
the hardware design.
Designing a case to test general usability and ergonomics, and
find issues with the mechanical design of the PCB.
The next revision will be focused on addressing issues from Rev1.
Known issues
The backlight cannot be disabled, power is supplied to the LEDs
even when the boost converter is disabled.
The current limit on the backlight LED driver is set too low
(20 mA paralleled to 4 LEDs, should be 20 mA per LED).
Reference designators in the schematics don't make much sense,
there are gaps in the numbering and samed-valued components are
not in contiguous ranges.
License
Unless otherwise noted, all files in this repository, including
this README, are available under the terms of the CERN-OHL-S
version 2 license, which should be found in the file
COPYING.txt
alongside this README; or at
https://ohwr.org/cern_ohl_s_v2.txt
.

data.author: solarmist
data.article_summary: 本文简要列出了与YouTube平台相关的多项信息和功能。内容包括关于YouTube的介绍、新闻发布、版权声明、联系方式、创作者信息、广告、开发者支持、条款规定、隐私政策、安全指南以及如何使用YouTube。此外，还提到正在测试的新功能和NFL Sunday Ticket服务，并注明版权归属2025年谷歌公司。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Modular.ai的潜在发展、GPU编程的挑战及相关技术选择

不同观点：
• [支持Modular.ai的立场] solarmist认为Modular.ai有可能成功，因为GPU编程（如CUDA）非常复杂，开发新语言可能是必要的，以解决当前的困难。
• [对CUDA及替代方案的现实看法] diabllicseagull承认脱离CUDA的愿望，但也指出，转向其他替代方案可能会带来新的财务负担，尤其是企业级许可。同时，开源方案由于功能有限和长期支持不确定，也未能让人完全放心。
• [对许可证的关注] Archit3ch关注Modular.ai许可证中的设备限制问题，特别是当用户数超过8个时（每个用户拥有一台设备），这种情况如何处理并不明确。
• [误解与期望落差] catapart原本期待的是图形编程API（如Metal、Vulkan或OpenGL）的革新，而非当前Modular.ai所专注的领域，因此感到失望。
• [对视频制作问题的反馈] ashvardanian提到视频中的一个“公开的秘密”，似乎是指视频中的某些内容值得特别关注。
• [对音频质量的批评] throwaway314155批评视频的音频质量问题，特别是噪音消除功能导致的声音切断和糟糕的音效。

补充讨论：
• 不同用户对Modular.ai的期望和关注点各不相同，有的关注其技术潜力，有的则对其商业模式和许可证细节提出疑问。
• 音频质量问题虽然与核心讨论点无关，但也是一个用户体验上的重要问题，值得注意。
• 对开源方案的信心不足反映了在技术社区中，长期支持和功能覆盖是选择替代技术时的重要考虑因素。

data.title: xPrize in Carbon Removal Goes to Enhanced Rock Weathering
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: Mati Carbon赢得了XPrize碳去除大赛，其创新方法利用了细碎的玄武岩来加速大气中二氧化碳的去除。通过增强岩石风化作用，该公司能够更有效地捕获和储存二氧化碳。此外，Mati Carbon的软件和数据收集系统也获得了评委的青睐，因其有助于监测和优化碳去除过程。该技术为应对气候变化提供了一种新的解决方案，展示了在碳捕集与储存领域的创新潜力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过在农田上铺设玄武岩粉来捕捉二氧化碳的可行性及效果

不同观点：
• **支持玄武岩粉铺设的观点**：  
  - 玄武岩粉富含硅酸盐矿物，能够通过风化作用与空气中的二氧化碳反应，生成碳酸氢盐离子，从而防止二氧化碳返回大气。  
  - 该方法不仅改善了农田土壤质量，还具备碳捕捉的功能，是一种双赢的环保策略。

• **关于释放环境的选择**：  
  - **释放到雨 storms**：有人认为雨水中含有溶解的二氧化碳，玄武岩粉在雨中的反应可能更有效，因为雨水的酸性有助于加速岩石的风化过程，从而更快速地捕捉空气中的二氧化碳。  
  - **直接释放到大气中**：另一观点则提出直接将玄武岩粉释放到大气中是否更有效，但该观点尚未深入探讨其实际效果，仅作为问题提出。

补充讨论：
• **技术可行性问题**：  
  - 虽然玄武岩粉的环境效益被认可，但其实际操作和分布方式仍需进一步探讨，特别是在大规模应用时，如何平衡成本与效益仍是一个问题。

• **争议焦点**：  
  - 主要的争议在于玄武岩粉的释放方式是否会影响其碳捕捉的效果，尤其是在大气中和雨水中两种不同环境下的比较。目前没有明确结论，需要更多的实验数据支撑。

data.title: General anesthesia reduces uniqueness of brain's functional 'fingerprint'
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了麦吉尔大学和剑桥大学等研究机构的一项研究，探讨全身麻醉对大脑独特功能连接模式的影响。研究发现，全身麻醉抑制了大脑独特的功能连接模式，使得不同个体的大脑活动变得相似，难以区分，而在清醒状态下，个体间的大脑活动模式是独特的，可以通过"脑指纹"进行区分。研究使用了功能磁共振成像（fMRI）技术，对比了志愿者在清醒、麻醉期间和恢复意识后的脑活动。结果显示，麻醉尤其影响了人类独有的脑区活动。这项研究有助于理解麻醉对大脑的影响，并可能为昏迷患者意识恢复的治疗提供启示。研究发表在《Nature Human Behaviour》上。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：全身麻醉对身体和认知的长期影响

不同观点：
• [aught] 分享了个人经历，提到在两次全身麻醉手术后，没有出现认知能力下降，但失去了味觉，且有异常的感知体验（如认为食物有毒，味道变质或化学味）。尽管医生表示不用担心，并称味觉可能会在六个月后恢复，但这种体验让他非常震惊。

• [omneity] 对文章中关于全身麻醉导致失去意识时“脑指纹”变化的讨论表示不满，认为文章过于关注轶事而缺乏深入的科学见解，并强调更应关注脑指纹在失去意识期间的变化这一核心问题。

• [pixelpoet] 指出文章（未阅读原始研究论文）并未表明麻醉后的脑指纹会永久改变，并认为标题可能误导读者以为这种变化是长期的。

• [Bluescreenbuddy] 分享了个人经历，提到自己经历了五次全身麻醉，并对麻醉是否已经对自己产生了长期影响表示疑问和担忧。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于全身麻醉是否会对大脑功能和感知（如味觉、认知能力等）产生长期或永久的影响。部分用户（如[aught]）提供了个人案例，显示麻醉后出现了味觉异常，而其他用户（如[pixelpoet]）则认为文章没有明确说明这些变化是否是永久性的。

• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是[omneity]对文章内容的不满，认为文章过于依赖轶事而未深入探讨麻醉对脑指纹的科学影响，显示出对更深入科学分析的需求。

General anesthesia reduces uniqueness of brain's functional 'fingerprint,' study finds
by Ingrid Fadelli                                                                                , Medical Xpress
Anatomical characterization of contributions to sevoflurane-induced loss of functional identifiability. Credit:
Nature Human Behaviour
(2025). DOI: 10.1038/s41562-025-02121-9
Past psychology research suggests that different people display characteristic patterns of spontaneous thought, emotions and behaviors. These patterns make the brains of distinct individuals unique, to the point that neuroscientists can often tell them apart based on their neural activity.
Researchers at McGill University, University of Cambridge and other institutes recently carried out a study aimed at investigating how general anesthesia influences the unique neural activity signatures that characterize the brains of different people and animals.
Their findings,
published
in
Nature Human Behavior
, show that general anesthesia suppresses each brain's unique functional connectivity patterns (i.e., the connections and communication patterns between different regions of the brain), both in humans and other species.
"Every person is unique, they think and feel and act in unique ways," Andrea Luppi, first author of the paper, told Medical Xpress. "This uniqueness comes from our brain. The way that areas of the brain interact with each other is unique to each individual: it can be used like a 'brain fingerprint.'
"But when you lose consciousness, for example during
deep sleep
, your sense of being 'you' is gone. So, our question was: what happens to brain fingerprints when we lose consciousness, such as during the artificial sleep induced by general anesthesia? "
To explore the effects of anesthesia on the brain's functional connectivity patterns, Luppi and his colleagues employed an imaging technique commonly used in
neuroscience research
called functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI). This technique allows neuroscientists to monitor the activity of different
brain regions
over time and non-invasively, by measuring changes in blood flow.
"We collected fMRI scans from healthy human volunteers before general anesthesia, then when they were unconscious because of the anesthesia, and then again after they recovered consciousness," explained Luppi. "For each scan, we measured 'functional connectivity': a representation of how brain regions interact. We used this functional connectivity to obtain 'brain fingerprints,' telling us how easy or difficult it is to tell people apart based on their
brain activity
."
Interestingly, the fMRI scans collected by the researchers showed that the brain activity of people while they were under the influence of anesthesia was suppressed. In fact, anesthesia made people almost impossible to tell apart from each other solely by examining their brain activity, which was possible when they were still conscious.
"In contrast, using brain fingerprints it is very easy to tell people apart when they are conscious," said Luppi. "This effect is not uniform in the brain: it is strongest in the parts of the brain that are uniquely human and mostly distinguish us from other species. The implication is that just as your own conscious experience is unique to you, so are the brain patterns that support it. When consciousness is gone, people's brain activity is also less unique."
Luppi and his colleagues gathered interesting new insights about the effects of general anesthesia on the brain and its unique patterns of
neural activity
. In the future, the results of their study could inspire further cross-species research looking at the brain before, during and after the administration of anesthetics, which could in turn inform the development of interventions to facilitate the rehabilitation of both people and animals after medical procedures that require anesthesia.
"I am very interested in comparisons between humans and other species," added Luppi. "Anesthesia is very conserved across species, so we can learn a lot from them about how anesthesia works on the brain. Ultimately, I hope that by learning how the brain reboots consciousness after
anesthesia
, we can learn how to help recovery of
consciousness
in patients who suffer from coma and other forms of chronic unconsciousness after a brain injury."
More information:
Andrea I. Luppi et al, General anaesthesia decreases the uniqueness of brain functional connectivity across individuals and species,
Nature Human Behaviour
(2025).
